Subject: Performance SLO / Benchmark methodology 1 prompt sets & eval harness

Hi Alex / Priya 1

Thanks again for the time today 1 the discovery was super helpful. Below is a short recap and next steps so we can align on a reproducible benchmark for your latency/throughput SLOs.

Recap (short):
- Target latency SLOs: 95th percentile <= 250ms for single-turn generation at 512 tokens (streaming enabled)
- Throughput: expected sustained throughput 600 requests/min with concurrency spikes to 1200 RPS during market open windows
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 80-120 per model shard, peaking at ~400 in extreme cases
- Streaming: client requires token-by-token streaming + chunked JSON outputs for partial results

Requested deliverables from Redwood:
1) Benchmark methodology doc with prompt sets + eval harness we can run (reproducible)
2) Measurement definitions (p95/p99 latency, tail-latency calculation, throughput under closed-loop vs open-loop)
3) A sample prompt set that reflects your production traffic (few-shot prompts & edge-case prompts)
4) Guidance on env parity (quantization, GPU type, batch config) and how results translate to hosted vs Dedicated

Attached: preliminary prompt set (edgefin_benchmark_prompts_v1.csv), a short README for our eval harness (redwood_eval_harness_readme.md), and a strawman SLO definition table (slo_definition_table.xlsx).

Next steps:
- Internal: Dev will review the prompt set and confirm harness parameters (Dev: can you call out any missing telemetry we should capture?)
- External: Alex / Priya, please confirm the three representative traffic profiles (normal / market-open / peak) by EOD Tuesday and share any additional prompt examples you want included.
- I'll schedule a follow-up to run a joint benchmark (we can do a dry-run on our side first) 1 proposed slots Wed/Thu next week.

Thanks 1 talk soon.

11
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Benchmark methodology 1 prompt sets & eval harness

Thanks Marissa 1 really clear, appreciate the artifacts. Quick clarifications from our side:

1) The 250ms p95 target is for end-to-end response (first token) from client to first-streamed token, correct? We need that clarified for procurement.
2) Throughput: our 600 requests/min is an average sustained rate across a set of ~12 trading microservices. During market open we expect bursts closer to 1200 req/min for a 10-15 minute window.
3) Streaming: yes 1 first-token latency is the most critical. We also care about per-token inter-arrival times for streaming when responses exceed 256 tokens.

We'll review the prompt set and send a couple of live examples (redacted) by tomorrow. Also 1 for the benchmark environment: what GPU family are you using for the hosted numbers vs what you recommend for Dedicated?

Appreciate it 1 Alex
Head of Platform, EdgeFin Capital
alex.turner@edgefin.com | +1 617 555 0199

Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Benchmark methodology 1 prompt sets & eval harness

Hi Alex / Priya 1

Quick technical notes to address Alex's Qs and to make sure the harness will capture the right telemetry:

- Latency definition: we'll report "time-to-first-byte (TTFB) of first token" as primary (p50/p95/p99). We'll also report "time-to-last-byte" for full generations. For streaming we'll include inter-token 95th percentiles over the token stream.
- Environment parity: Hosted baseline numbers were measured on A100 80GB (mixed precision) with Redwood's streaming-optimized runtime. For Dedicated recommendations, we typically validate on A10/A100 families depending on cost: A100 for peak low-latency, A10 for cost-optimized throughput. We'll include both translation tables in the README.
- Measurement modes: closed-loop (client waits for response before next request) for latency-focused runs; open-loop (constant arrival process) for throughput characterization. We'll run both for each traffic profile.
- Telemetry we'll capture per request: request_id, arrival_ts, first_token_ts, last_token_ts, token_count, model_variant, batch_size, GPU_type, concurrency_at_arrival. Logs will be exportable as JSONL.

Attached is a short RFC to the harness README with suggested metrics and a sample JSONL schema. Dev

[Inline: excerpt from redwood_eval_harness_readme.md]

Alex 1 thanks for the quick reply and great questions. A few follow-ups:

- Confirming: p95 <= 250ms refers to time-to-first-token (what Dev called TTFB). We'll make that explicit in the SLO column.
- GPU: we'll include the mapping table. For the joint benchmark run we can use an A100-equivalent config so numbers translate directly to your Dedicated projection. If you'd like a cost-focused baseline we can also run on A10 and include both sets.
- Streaming inter-token: we'll capture median and p95 inter-token intervals for responses >256 tokens and include a plot in the final report.

Can you confirm the following by EOD Tue as mentioned: three traffic profiles and any additional prompt examples? Once we have that, Rishi and I will schedule a 90-minute joint run window and share a pre-run checklist (network perf, warmup, seed model weights).

Also copying Rishi since he may request additional access for test keys or a sandbox workspace.

11
Marissa
